subject: Post-demo: FastHealth buying workflow & latency/cost guardrails
messages:
From: kimberly.park@redwood.com
To: michael.jensen@fasthealth.com, ellen.cho@fasthealth.com
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap + next steps (latency / procurement map)

Hi Michael / Ellen —

Thanks again for your time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

1) Key decision criteria we heard from the call:
   - Latency target: p95 generation latency <= 150ms for 512-token prompts in production (mobile clients)
   - Cost guidance: prefer incremental token cost < $0.003/token equivalent for our primary endpoint (inference + cache)
   - Deployment preference: start on Redwood Dedicated for predictable throughput; evaluate Private (VPC) for PHI pilot if legal requires
   - SLA: 99.9% uptime target; RTO for major incidents: 2 hours

2) Stakeholder map (what we heard):
   - Economic buyer: likely Michael Jensen (Head of AI) — will confirm
   - Security & compliance: Samir Khan (Security) — expects SOC 2 + data residency details
   - Procurement/legal: Elena Ruiz — will handle PO/contract templates and timing
   - Product owner: Ellen Cho — owns rollout timing and P1 targets

3) Proposed mutual action items:
   - We (Redwood) to share SOC 2 summary + short M&A (attachment) and a Mutual Action Plan XLS with timelines (attached).
   - FastHealth to confirm the economic buyer and procurement timeline by next Tue (16 Mar).
   - Quick follow-up 30-min call to walk procurement through pricing bands and SLA options; proposed Tue 16 Mar 10:00am PT — please confirm.

If any of those callouts are off, tell me now and I’ll update. Otherwise I’ll send the MAP and SOC2 summary right after this.

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0148

Attachments: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (summary), FastHealth-mutual-action-plan.xlsx (draft MAP)

From: michael.jensen@fasthealth.com
To: kimberly.park@redwood.com
Cc: ellen.cho@fasthealth.com, procurement@fasthealth.com, security@fasthealth.com
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + next steps (latency / procurement map)

Kimberly —

Thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side before we lock dates: 

- Latency: 150ms p95 is our preferred goal for customer-facing inference, but for the first pilot we can accept up to 250ms while we instrument caching and SDK-side batching. Would Redwood be able to guarantee 150ms for Dedicated in the baseline config you showed?

- Cost: the $0.003/token equivalent is within range, but our finance team will need a predictable blended rate (inference + egress) for forecasting. Can you provide sample blended monthly scenarios for 100k, 1M, and 5M tokens?

- Procurement & legal: Elena (procurement@fasthealth.com) — we typically need 45 days for PO and standard SLAs; if there are non-standard liabilities we escalate to legal. Samir (security@fasthealth.com) — can you share the security questionnaire we should expect?

We can do the Tue 16 Mar 10:00am PT call — Ellen will join. See procurement & security on copy to share their availability.

—Michael
Michael Jensen
Head of AI, FastHealth
michael.jensen@fasthealth.com

Hi Kimberly / Michael —

Thanks for looping procurement. A couple of process notes from our side: 

- Procurement timeline: 45 days from receipt of final SOW / pricing. We need the following to start:
   * Final pricing table (unit rates and discounts by commit level)
   * Proposed MSA and SOW redlines (we prefer trackable Word docs)
   * Contact for contractual negotiations

- Internal approvals: we will route to Legal for indemnity/liability review and to Finance for budgeting. If Redwood needs accelerated approval, please flag any special terms now.

- Attachments/security: Samir, can you confirm whether SOC 2 Type II plus standard audit reports suffice for your security review? If not, we will request any additional artifacts through our secure transfer.

We will be present on Tue 16 Mar 10:00am PT.

procurement@fasthealth.com

From: kimberly.park@redwood.com
To: michael.jensen@fasthealth.com, procurement@fasthealth.com, security@fasthealth.com, ellen.cho@fasthealth.com
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com, dev.patel@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + next steps (latency / procurement map)

Thanks all — confirmed for Tue 16 Mar 10:00am PT (calendar invite sent).

Quick answers ahead of the call so procurement/legal have something to work with: 

- Latency guarantee: For Redwood Dedicated with the model configuration we demoed (quantized 8-bit, KV caching enabled, continuous batching), we can commit to p95 <= 150ms at steady-state for 512-token workloads under a baseline commit of 10 dedicated GPUs. If FastHealth wants an SLA that guarantees 150ms under arbitrary traffic spikes, that requires an elevated commit level or burst capacity (we can include that as an SLA option).

- Cost scenarios (blended rate examples, tokens/month -> estimated blended unit cost):
   * 100k tokens/month -> ~$0.0045/token
   * 1M tokens/month -> ~$0.0028/token
   * 5M tokens/month -> ~$0.0019/token
   (These are blended examples including inference, KV cache hit assumptions, and standard egress; we will provide a spreadsheet with detailed line items on the call.)

- Contracting: Point of contact for negotiations: lauren.bishop@redwood.com (cc'd). We will share a Word SOW and redlineable MSA today.

Action items I will complete before the call:
   - Upload the detailed pricing scenarios and a short note explaining the assumptions (cache hit rate 60%, average prompt length 220 tokens).
   - Share SOC 2 Type II summary and a short runbook on data handling (attached earlier).

If that looks good we’ll use the call to walk procurement through the spreadsheet and confirm the PO timeline.

See you shortly —
Kim
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com

Attachments: pricing_scenarios_FastHealth.xlsx (to be uploaded to Drive)
